findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query, so the cache status UI stays stale after deletion
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess?.()`. The `disconnectMutation` explicitly invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `utils.viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`, but the delete-cache mutation does not. After a successful cache deletion, the `connectedCalendars` query still returns the old `cacheUpdatedAt`, so the dropdown continues to show "Cache Status: Last updated ..." and the "Delete cached data" option even though the cache rows were deleted. The component relies on the parent's `onChanged` callback to refetch, but `onChanged` is optional and in `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` it is passed through from props without any guaranteed invalidation. The mutation should invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (at minimum) in `onSettled`, mirroring the disconnect mutation.

findings.title: Confirmation dialog closes immediately on confirm, before the mutation completes, so failures leave no visible feedback path
findings.body: In both confirmation dialogs, `onConfirm` calls `mutation.mutate(...)` and then unconditionally `setDeleteModalOpen(false)` / `setDisconnectModalOpen(false)`. The dialog closes immediately while the mutation is still in flight. If the mutation fails, the only feedback is the error toast; the user cannot retry from the dialog and there is no pending/loading state on the confirm button. This is a UX robustness issue: a transient network error forces the user to reopen the dropdown and repeat the flow. Consider keeping the dialog open (with a loading state on the confirm button) until the mutation settles, as is common with `ConfirmationDialogContent` usage elsewhere.

findings.title: Hardcoded 'en-US' locale for cache timestamp formatting ignores the user's locale
findings.body: The cache timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })`. The component already uses `useLocale()` for translations, so the user's locale is available but not used here. Non-English users will see dates in US format, inconsistent with the rest of the app which formats dates according to the user's locale. The formatter should use the locale from `useLocale()` (e.g. `const { t, i18n } = useLocale()` and `i18n.language` or the dayjs locale used elsewhere in the codebase).

findings.title: Cache status row is rendered as an interactive DropdownMenuItem with no action, trapping keyboard focus on a non-actionable element
findings.body: The cache status display (lines 84-97) is wrapped in a `<DropdownMenuItem className="focus:ring-muted">` even though it performs no action — it is purely informational. Radix `DropdownMenuItem` is an interactive menu item: it is focusable, responds to Enter/Space, and shows hover/active states, which misleads users into thinking it is clickable. It should be a non-interactive element (e.g. a plain `<div>` with appropriate padding, or `DropdownMenuLabel`/`DropdownMenuSeparator` semantics) so keyboard and screen-reader users are not stuck on a dead item. Nesting a `<div>` inside `DropdownMenuItem` also produces a menu item whose accessible name is the concatenated text, which is acceptable, but the interactivity is the real problem.

findings.title: connectedCalendars now always instantiates CalendarCacheRepository and runs an extra groupBy query even when calendar-cache is disabled
findings.body: The handler unconditionally constructs `new CalendarCacheRepository()` and calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(credentialIds)` on every `connectedCalendars` query. The codebase has a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` used precisely when the calendar-cache feature is disabled (the mock logs "Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled"), and `CalendarCache.init(null)` elsewhere selects mock vs. real based on configuration. Here the real repository is always used, so every connectedCalendars call — including for users/teams without the calendar-cache feature — pays for an extra `groupBy` DB query. This adds latency to a frequently-called query (it is used with `suspense: true` in the settings UI and onboarding). The handler should use the same feature-detection used by `CalendarCache.init` (e.g. check the team feature flag / `getCalendarCacheRepository()` factory) and skip the query entirely when the feature is disabled, returning `cacheUpdatedAt: null`.

findings.title: credentialIds may contain in-memory delegation credential ids (negative numbers) which are passed to a DB groupBy query
findings.body: `connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId)` can include negative in-memory delegation credential ids (the codebase uses negative ids for in-memory delegation credentials, see `isInMemoryDelegationCredential` and `assertCalendarHasDbCredential` which throws for `credentialId < 0`). These ids are passed straight into `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy({ where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } } })`. Prisma will happily query with negative integers (no rows match), so this is not a crash, but it is wasted work and signals the handler does not account for delegation credentials. The `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` call should filter to DB-backed credential ids (e.g. `credentialIds.filter(id => id > 0)`) or the repository should guard, consistent with `assertCalendarHasDbCredential` used elsewhere in the same package.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object, relying on Prisma @updatedAt side effect with no explicit intent
findings.body: `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object. The only effect is that Prisma touches `updatedAt` (because the schema has `@updatedAt` on SelectedCalendar). This is obscure: a reader cannot tell whether the empty object is a bug or intentional. The PR description itself notes "Consider if SelectedCalendar.updatedAt update should be removed." Either make the intent explicit with a comment or pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` explicitly, or remove the call if the timestamp is not consumed anywhere (the frontend uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache, not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt).

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId accepts Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput but the only caller passes {}, hiding the fact that it can update arbitrary fields across all of a credential's calendars
findings.body: The new method signature is `updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId: number, data: Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput)`. `SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` allows updating any scalar field (externalId, integration, userId, eventTypeId, googleChannelId, etc.) across every SelectedCalendar row for a credential. That is a broad, potentially dangerous primitive (e.g. it could reassign calendars to another userId or change externalId en masse). The only current caller passes `{}`, so the method's real purpose is "touch updatedAt". The signature should be narrowed to reflect actual intent — e.g. `updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId: number)` that internally sets `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`, or accept a restricted `Pick<Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, "updatedAt">` — so future callers cannot accidentally mass-modify integrity-sensitive fields.

findings.title: Migration adds updatedAt with DEFAULT NOW() but the Prisma schema comment claims it provides a value for 'future raw inserts' — the default is not persisted in the schema, so raw inserts after migration will fail
findings.body: The migration uses `ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW();`. In Postgres, `DEFAULT NOW()` is a persistent column default, so raw SQL inserts without `updatedAt` will work. However, the schema comment says "Provide an initial value for legacy rows and future raw inserts" while the Prisma schema defines `updatedAt DateTime @default(now()) @updatedAt` — Prisma's `@default(now())` is applied by the Prisma client, not the database, so the migration's `DEFAULT NOW()` and Prisma's default are two different mechanisms. The real risk: the migration's warning text says the column was added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty" — but the SQL does provide a default, so the warning is stale/incorrect (likely hand-edited after generation). More importantly, if this migration is ever squashed or the default is dropped, raw inserts break. The migration comment/warning should be corrected to reflect that a default IS provided, and the team should verify the default persists (it does in Postgres, but the misleading warning suggests the migration was manually edited and may not match what `prisma migrate dev` would generate).

findings.title: Stale TODO comment says updatedAt 'doesn't exist yet in CalendarCache table' but the column was just added by this PR
findings.body: Line 116 contains `// TODO: For better tracking we could also want to use updatedAt directly which doesn't exist yet in CalendarCache table`. This PR adds the `updatedAt` column to CalendarCache (schema.prisma + migration). The TODO is now obsolete: `updatedAt` exists and is exactly what `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` uses. The ordering logic in `getCachedAvailability` (orderBy `expiresAt: "desc"`) could now also consider `updatedAt`, or the TODO should be removed/updated so future readers are not misled into thinking the column is missing.

findings.title: sed -i '' is macOS-only and will break on Linux CI/dev machines
findings.body: Line 68 uses `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"`. The `-i ''` syntax is the BSD/macOS form of in-place sed; on GNU/Linux `sed -i ''` treats `''` as a file name and fails with "can't read : No such file or directory". Since this is a developer helper script committed to the repo (not a macOS-only tool), it should use a portable form such as `sed -i.bak -E ... && rm -f "$ENV_FILE.bak"` or detect the platform. As written, the script silently corrupts or fails to update `.env` on Linux.

findings.title: Script writes a public tunnel URL into ../.env, potentially committing a webhook endpoint that exposes the local Google Calendar webhook to the internet
findings.body: The script sets `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` in `../.env` to a public `*.tunnelmole.net` URL. The Google Calendar webhook handler at `/api/integrations/googlecalendar/webhook` is protected by `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`, but this script's purpose is to expose a local dev server to Google's push notifications. Risks: (1) the tunnel URL is written into a file that developers may accidentally commit (`.env` is typically gitignored, but `../.env` relative to `scripts/` is the repo-root `.env` — verify it is ignored); (2) the tunnel stays alive for the whole script session, leaving a public route into the developer's machine; (3) the script reuses an already-running tmole (`pgrep -f "tmole $TM_PORT"`) without verifying it belongs to this project, potentially overwriting `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` for an unrelated tunnel. At minimum the script should warn that the tunnel is public and ensure `.env` is gitignored.

findings.title: Fixed w-32 container may clip or misalign the new dropdown trigger compared to the previous DisconnectIntegration button
findings.body: The actions container is `<div className="flex w-32 justify-end">` wrapping `CredentialActionsDropdown`, whose trigger is an icon-only `Button` with `StartIcon="ellipsis"`. The previous `DisconnectIntegration` with `trashIcon` rendered a similarly small icon button, so width is probably fine, but `w-32` (8rem) is a hardcoded width sized for the old control. If `CredentialActionsDropdown` returns `null` (when `!canDisconnect && !hasCache`, e.g. a delegation credential with no cache), the `w-32` div still renders as an empty 8rem-wide block, leaving a visible gap on the right side of every credential card. The wrapper should render nothing (or not fix the width) when the dropdown is absent — e.g. let `CredentialActionsDropdown` own its container, or conditionally render the wrapper div.

findings.title: Cache actions are gated only on integrationType === google_calendar, but any credential with cache rows (e.g. after an integration rename or a different cached provider) would be hidden; conversely the check does not verify the cache feature is enabled
findings.body: `hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` means the "Delete cached data" action only appears for Google Calendar credentials that have a non-null `cacheUpdatedAt`. Two issues: (1) The server enriches `cacheUpdatedAt` for ALL credentials (the groupBy is not filtered by integration), so if cache rows ever exist for a non-Google credential (e.g. a future cached provider, or leftover rows), the UI silently hides the delete action while the server still reports a timestamp — the user has no way to clear it. (2) The gating on `integrationType === GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TYPE` is a UI-level assumption that duplicates server knowledge; the server should be the source of truth for whether cache management applies. The condition should be based on `cacheUpdatedAt` presence alone (server-controlled), or the server should only populate `cacheUpdatedAt` for integrations where cache deletion is supported.

findings.title: deleteCache input schema is defined inline instead of a dedicated schema file, inconsistent with sibling procedures
findings.body: The router defines `deleteCache` with an inline `z.object({ credentialId: z.number() })`, while `connectedCalendars` and `setDestinationCalendar` import dedicated schemas (`ZConnectedCalendarsInputSchema`, `ZSetDestinationCalendarInputSchema`) from `./connectedCalendars.schema` and `./setDestinationCalendar.schema`. The codebase convention (visible in the same file) is one schema file per procedure. This inconsistency makes the input schema harder to discover/reuse (e.g. for platform API parity or client-side validation) and will drift from the handler's `DeleteCacheOptions` type, which is declared separately in `deleteCache.handler.ts` with no compile-time link to the zod schema. Create `deleteCache.schema.ts` exporting `ZDeleteCacheInputSchema` and use it in both the router and the handler type (`z.infer<typeof ZDeleteCacheInputSchema>`).

findings.title: Unrelated refactor of findMany (removing satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs) is bundled into this PR
findings.body: The diff changes `findMany` from building `const args = { where, select, orderBy } satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs; return await prisma.selectedCalendar.findMany(args);` to a direct `return await prisma.selectedCalendar.findMany({ where, select, orderBy });`. This change is unrelated to the calendar-cache feature (it removes a type-safety assertion). It is not needed for the feature and slightly reduces type checking strictness; it should be reverted or split into its own PR so reviewers can evaluate it independently.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds does not guard against an empty credentialIds array, issuing a pointless groupBy query
findings.body: When `connectedCalendars` is empty (a user with no connected calendar apps, or all filtered out by `_ensureNoConflictingNonDelegatedConnectedCalendar`), `credentialIds` is `[]` and the handler still calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds([])`, which issues `SELECT credentialId, MAX(updatedAt) FROM CalendarCache WHERE credentialId IN () GROUP BY credentialId`. Prisma translates `IN ()` to a `FALSE`/`0 = 1` condition, so the query is cheap but still a round-trip to the DB on every connectedCalendars call for users with no calendars. The repository method (or the handler) should early-return `[]` when `credentialIds.length === 0`.

findings.title: cacheUpdatedAt prop is typed as Date but tRPC serializes dates as strings over the wire with superjson disabled or as Date with superjson — type may mismatch at runtime
findings.body: The prop is `cacheUpdatedAt?: Date | null` and the component does `new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)` before formatting, which works for both Date and string. However, the tRPC `RouterOutputs` type for `connectedCalendars` will type `cacheUpdatedAt` according to the transformer. Cal.com uses superjson, which preserves Date instances, so the type is likely correct. But the defensive `new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)` suggests uncertainty. If the transformer ever changes or the platform atoms package consumes this without superjson, the `Date` type would be a lie and `Intl.DateTimeFormat.format()` would receive a string (which `new Date()` handles, so it works). This is a minor robustness note: either trust the type and drop the `new Date()` wrapper, or type the prop as `Date | string | null` to be explicit. Low severity because the current code handles both.

findings.title: New locale strings are added only to en/common.json; all other locales are missing the keys, causing fallback or raw-key display for non-English users
findings.body: The PR adds 7 new keys (`cache_status`, `cache_last_updated`, `delete_cached_data`, `cache_deleted_successfully`, `error_deleting_cache`, `confirm_delete_cache`, `yes_delete_cache`) only to the English locale file. Cal.com's i18n setup (next-i18next with `ADD_NEW_STRINGS_ABOVE_THIS_LINE_TO_PREVENT_MERGE_CONFLICTS`) expects translations to be contributed for other locales, typically via the `translate-locales` script or Crowdin. Until other locales are updated, non-English users will see either the English fallback or the raw key (depending on `fallbackLng` config). This is a known workflow in the repo, but the PR should either run the translation pipeline or note that translations are pending. At minimum, verify the fallback behavior so users don't see raw keys like `cache_deleted_successfully`.
